title: Unit 7: The World of Mass Media

lessons.title: Language: Adverbial clauses with as if / as though
objectives: Nắm vững các khái niệm và định nghĩa cốt lõi của Language: Adverbial clauses with as if / as though.
Hiểu và áp dụng thành thạo các quy tắc và công thức trong SGK 12.
Rèn luyện kỹ năng phân tích và giải quyết các bài toán/tình huống thực tiễn ôn thi THPT & ĐGNL.

concepts.definition: Used to describe how a situation seems. If expressing an untrue/hypothetical situation in the present, use Past Simple/were; if referring to an untrue situation in the past, use Past Perfect (had V3).
concepts.example: He speaks about digital privacy as if he were an expert (in reality he is not).
concepts.essence: Distinguishing between realistic appearance and counterfactual pretense.

concepts.definition: The ability to critically access, analyze, evaluate, and create media messages in various formats, discerning verified facts from biased propaganda or fabricated misinformation.
concepts.example: Checking author credentials and reverse image searching before sharing controversial news headlines.
concepts.essence: Cognitive defense mechanism against information manipulation in the digital age.

rules.statement: Subjunctive mood after 'as if / as though'
rules.meaning: When the comparison is contrary to present fact, 'were' is conventionally used for all persons (as if I were, as if he were).
rules.example: She acted as though she knew nothing about the incident.
rules.essence: Formal grammatical signaling of counterfactual reality.

workedExamples.prompt: Put the verb into correct form: 'The boy speaks English fluently as if he (live) in London for years (in fact he has never been abroad).'
steps: Step 1: Check reality: he has never been abroad -> the situation is unreal/hypothetical in relation to the present.
Step 2: Expressing an unreal completed past experience -> use Past Perfect: had lived.
Step 3: Assemble sentence: The boy speaks English fluently as if he had lived in London for years.

commonMistakes.mistake: Confusing real comparisons with unreal comparisons: *It looks as if it rained* when clouds are actually dark.
commonMistakes.why: If something is likely or true, use real tenses: It looks as if it is going to rain.
